rationale: Adds a test-only emitter conformance gate (four committed DesignIR fixtures built through the native materializer, the ui.js bridge program, the baked C++ exporter generated at build time by a test tool, and the SwiftUI exporter, compared against an allowlist of known gaps) and a development-only ui.js lane for the differential lab: pulp-design-ir-observe --emitter js renders the candidate IR through the program generate_pulp_js() emits, and the lab passes the option through and records it. No shipped importer, emitter or renderer behavior changes; Chromium stays the only oracle and Skia/Dawn the renderer, so no design-import, Chromium, rendering, or packaging authority moves.
